title: The Deity of Christ
sourceBasis: World English Bible — 66-book Old and New Testament Scripture text already installed in Iron Sharpener
definition: The deity of Christ means that Jesus Christ is truly God. He is not a created being, lesser divine figure, or merely an exalted teacher, but the eternal Son who shares the nature, glory, authority, and worship belonging to God alone.
summary: The deity of Christ means that Jesus Christ is truly God. He is not a created being, lesser divine figure, or merely an exalted teacher, but the eternal Son who shares the nature, glory, authority, and worship belonging to God alone.
christFocus: Jesus reveals God because He is God the Son in human flesh. To see Him rightly is to see the Father’s glory, truth, grace, power, and saving purpose revealed through the Son.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Scripture presents Jesus Christ as truly God. He existed before creation, all things were made through Him, and in Him all things hold together. He is not part of creation; He is the divine Son through whom creation came into being.

The deity of Christ is shown in His names, works, authority, worship, and glory. He forgives sins, receives worship, rules over creation, sustains all things, reveals the Father, and is addressed as Lord and God. These are not honors given to a mere creature.

The Son became flesh without ceasing to be God. The incarnation did not reduce His deity; it revealed divine glory in humility. Jesus is fully God and fully man, able to reveal God perfectly and save sinners completely.

If Christ is not truly God, the Gospel collapses. A created savior could not bear the full weight of salvation, reveal God fully, receive worship rightly, or bring sinners into eternal life with God. Because Jesus is God the Son, His work is sufficient, His promises are sure, and His glory is worthy of all worship.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
Many people are willing to call Jesus a good teacher, prophet, healer, or moral example while refusing to worship Him as God. But Scripture does not leave that option open. A reduced Christ produces a reduced Gospel and a false hope.

This doctrine anchors Christian faith and worship. Believers do not trust a powerless helper or distant religious figure. They trust the eternal Son of God who came in grace, died for sinners, rose in victory, reigns in glory, and is worthy of full surrender.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Worship Jesus Christ as Lord and God. Do not lower Him to fit cultural comfort, religious compromise, or personal preference. Trust His authority, obey His Word, rest in His saving power, and proclaim Him as the eternal Son who alone is able to save.
